name: LOOP_START_ULL(func, schedule)
prose: Macro that generates the GOMP unsigned-long-long loop start entry points (GOMP_loop_ull_static_start, dynamic, guided and the nonmonotonic variants): int func(int up, unsigned long long lb, unsigned long long ub, unsigned long long str, unsigned long long chunk_sz, unsigned long long *p_lb, unsigned long long *p_ub). It computes the signed stride str2 = up ? (long long)str : -(long long)str and obtains the global thread id. The loop is entered only if (str > 0) ? (lb < ub) : (lb > ub); since str is unsigned, str > 0 holds for every non-zero str, so the test is lb < ub unless str == 0, and the direction comes from `up` only through str2. If the test is true it calls KMP_DISPATCH_INIT_ULL with the macro's schedule, lb, upper bound ub - 1 (str2 > 0) or ub + 1, stride str2, chunk_sz and a final argument (schedule != kmp_sch_static), then KMP_DISPATCH_NEXT_ULL to fill *p_lb and *p_ub; when that returns non-zero it adds 1 to *p_ub if str > 0 and subtracts 1 otherwise (again by the unsigned test), and returns the status. If the test is false it returns 0 and does not write *p_lb or *p_ub. In debug builds an assertion checks the returned stride equals str2.
note: openmp/runtime/src/kmp_gsupport.cpp:892-927. Reviewer (r15) RIGHT: the dispatch init is skipped when the range test fails (:906, :917-919) and the stride comes from up/str2 (:897, :908). Observation, not tested: the final `*p_ub += (str > 0) ? 1 : -1` at :915 uses the unsigned str, unlike LOOP_NEXT_ULL which uses the signed stride (:979).

name: LOOP_RUNTIME_START_ULL(func, schedule)
prose: Macro that generates the GOMP unsigned-long-long runtime-schedule loop start entry points (GOMP_loop_ull_runtime_start and the maybe-nonmonotonic / nonmonotonic runtime variants): int func(int up, unsigned long long lb, unsigned long long ub, unsigned long long str, unsigned long long *p_lb, unsigned long long *p_ub). It has no chunk argument: chunk_sz is a local 0. Otherwise it behaves like LOOP_START_ULL: str2 = up ? str : -str; the loop is entered only if (str > 0) ? (lb < ub) : (lb > ub) (for unsigned str this is lb < ub unless str == 0); then KMP_DISPATCH_INIT_ULL(schedule, lb, ub - 1 or ub + 1 depending on str2 > 0, str2, chunk_sz 0, TRUE) and KMP_DISPATCH_NEXT_ULL fill *p_lb and *p_ub, and on a non-zero status *p_ub is adjusted by +1 if str > 0, else -1; it returns the status. If the range test fails it returns 0 and leaves *p_lb and *p_ub unwritten.
note: openmp/runtime/src/kmp_gsupport.cpp:929-965; invocations openmp/runtime/src/kmp_gsupport.cpp:1010-1019. Reviewer (r15) RIGHT for the same reasons as LOOP_START_ULL (init skipped when the test fails, stride from str2).

name: __kmp_test_adaptive_lock
prose: Tries to acquire an adaptive (speculative) lock without blocking; returns 1 on success and 0 on failure. If __kmp_should_speculate (acquire_attempts & badness == 0) holds, it first tries __kmp_test_adaptive_lock_only, a hardware-transactional (RTM) attempt: on _XBEGIN_STARTED it checks the underlying queuing lock is free (aborting the transaction if not) and returns 1, meaning the lock is held speculatively inside the transaction, not actually acquired; after soft aborts it retries up to max_soft_retries, a hard abort stops retrying, and when speculation fails the badness is stepped ((badness << 1) | 1, unchanged if that would exceed max_badness) and 0 is returned to this function. If speculation is not tried or fails, acquire_attempts is incremented (a plain, non-atomic increment) and __kmp_test_queuing_lock on the underlying queuing lock decides: 1 (and a non-speculative-acquire statistic) if it was acquired, else 0. So a failing call can change acquire_attempts and badness; the lock itself is not changed on failure.
note: openmp/runtime/src/kmp_lock.cpp:2045-2062 with __kmp_should_speculate openmp/runtime/src/kmp_lock.cpp:1986-1992, __kmp_test_adaptive_lock_only openmp/runtime/src/kmp_lock.cpp:1997-2040, __kmp_step_badness openmp/runtime/src/kmp_lock.cpp:1975-1982, __kmp_test_queuing_lock openmp/runtime/src/kmp_lock.cpp:1303-1333. Reviewers RIGHT (rounds 1/2): failure increments acquire_attempts (:2053).

name: __kmp_test_adaptive_lock_with_checks
prose: Checked variant of the adaptive-lock test used for omp_test_lock. If lck->lk.qlk.initialized does not equal the lock's queuing-lock pointer it calls KMP_FATAL(LockIsUninitialized, "omp_test_lock"). It then calls __kmp_test_adaptive_lock (which may change acquire_attempts and badness even on failure); if that returns non-zero it stores gtid + 1 in lck->lk.qlk.owner_id (also after a speculative success) and returns the value; on 0 it returns 0 without changing owner_id. It does not check for a nestable lock used as a simple lock (unlike the plain queuing-lock checked variant).
note: openmp/runtime/src/kmp_lock.cpp:2064-2077. Reviewer (round 1) RIGHT: underlying test increments acquire_attempts on failure. Compare __kmp_test_queuing_lock_with_checks openmp/runtime/src/kmp_lock.cpp:1335-1351, which also tests nestable use.

name: __kmp_serial_fork_call
prose: Handles a fork when the region is to be serialized; its two returns (lines 1923 and 1931) both return FALSE, so it never reports a real fork. It calls __kmpc_serialized_parallel(loc, gtid) (and under OMPD sets the serial team's t_pkfn). Then by call_context: fork_context_intel: sets the serial team's t_ident; if ap is null it reverts the level increment (t_level--) and invokes the microtask with the parent team's argv, bracketing it with OMPT lightweight-taskteam link, implicit-task begin/end, parallel-end callbacks and unlink; if the microtask is __kmp_teams_master it uses the current (serial) team, sets t_invoke, copies argc arguments from the va_list into its argv, decrements t_level and calls invoker(gtid), then fires OMPT implicit-task end and parallel-end callbacks (no lightweight taskteam is linked or unlinked on this branch); otherwise it copies the arguments from the va_list into a local array and invokes the microtask with the same OMPT bracketing as the first case. fork_context_gnu: with OMPT enabled it initialises and links a lightweight taskteam (exit frame cleared) and returns FALSE without invoking the microtask and without firing OMPT callbacks, leaving the unlink to the caller. Any other call_context hits KMP_ASSERT2. After the intel branches it executes a memory barrier and returns FALSE.
note: openmp/runtime/src/kmp_runtime.cpp:1711-1932 (returns :1923 and :1931; teams branch :1807-1838; gnu branch :1908-1923). Reviewers RIGHT: GNU path returns without OMPT callbacks (original), teams branch fires OMPT callbacks without linking/unlinking a lightweight taskteam (r15).

name: __kmp_join_call
prose: Ends a parallel region for the primary thread (join). Normal path: records th_ident and, with OMPT, sets the overhead state (not for a serialized GNU region); unless exit_teams it joins the team with __kmp_internal_join and releases ITT stack ids, while with exit_teams it only sets th_task_state = 0 (so a join barrier is not run for exit_teams). Early return 1 (team serialized): if the thread is in a teams construct it increments t_level when level == th_teams_level or t_serialized when level == th_teams_level + 1 (increments, not decrements), then calls __kmpc_end_serialized_parallel; with OMPT it unlinks the lightweight taskteam for the GNU context and restores state; returns. Early return 2 (teams construct, not exit_teams, team's microtask is not __kmp_teams_master, and t_level == th_teams_level + 1): ends the OMPT implicit task and unlinks the lightweight taskteam, decrements t_level and t_active_level and the root's r_in_parallel, enlarges t_nproc and the workers' th_team_nproc up to the teams size when th_team_nproc is smaller (initialising barrier state and task state of the added threads), fires the OMPT join callback, and returns with the team intact (it is not freed and the primary thread is not moved to the parent team). Otherwise (full join): restores the primary thread's tid, this_construct and dispatch pointer, takes __kmp_forkjoin_lock, decrements r_in_parallel only if not in a teams construct or t_level > th_teams_level, ends the OMPT implicit task, pops the current task, restores the default allocator and HW floating-point control, restores r_active when it differs, frees the team with __kmp_free_team (which frees worker threads), moves th_team, th_team_nproc, th_team_master, th_team_serialized to the parent team, frees and replaces the serial team if the parent is a serialized team other than the thread's serial team or the root team, restores task state and task team when tasking is enabled, marks the current task executing, releases the lock, resets the root init mask when the new level is 0 and affinity reset is set, and fires the OMPT join callback. Returns nothing.

Reviewer (original) RIGHT: exit_teams skips __kmp_internal_join (:2523-2540). Reviewer (r15) RIGHT: the serialized+teams path increments t_level/t_serialized (:2499, :2504).

name: __kmp_get_ancestor_thread_num
prose: Returns the thread number of the calling thread's ancestor at nesting level `level`, for global thread id gtid (assumed valid). Returns 0 if level == 0; -1 if level < 0; -1 if level is greater than the current team's t_level. Inside a teams construct (th_teams_microtask set) with level <= th_teams_level it first adjusts the local level counter ii (by +2 when ii == th_teams_level, else +1). If ii == level it returns the calling thread's own tid (__kmp_tid_from_gtid(gtid)). Otherwise it walks up parent teams, tracking the serialized depth dd, until the level is reached, and returns 0 if dd > 1, else that team's t_master_tid (the tid of the primary thread of the child region in the parent). Reads thread and team state only.
note: openmp/runtime/src/kmp_runtime.cpp:3058-3114 (returns :3069, :3071, :3076, :3095, :3113). Reviewers RIGHT: level < -1 also returns -1 (round 1), level > nesting returns -1, and the equal-level case returns the calling thread's tid, not the primary tid (round 2).

name: __kmp_parse_affinity_proc_id_list
prose: Parses a processor-id list string (GOMP_CPU_AFFINITY / explicit proclist style) starting at env; var names the variable for warnings. Sets *proclist = NULL first. Accepts comma-separated items with optional blanks: a decimal number n, a range n-m with an optional :stride (stride may be negative), or a braced set {n,n,...} (the first number after '{' is required). Returns FALSE after a KMP_WARNING on: a missing digit where one is required (AffSyntaxError), including a first token that is neither digit nor '{' when nothing has been parsed yet, stride 0 (AffZeroStride), start > end with positive stride (AffStartGreaterEnd), start < end with negative stride (AffStrideLessZero), or (end - start) / stride > 65536 (AffRangeTooBig); on FALSE *nextEnv is not written and *proclist stays NULL. Scanning stops at end of string or at a non-digit following at least one valid item (not an error). On TRUE it sets *nextEnv to the position where parsing stopped and *proclist to a newly allocated (__kmp_allocate) NUL-terminated copy of env[0 .. stop); an empty string yields TRUE with an empty copy. Numbers are parsed with __kmp_str_to_int; the code asserts they are non-negative.
note: openmp/runtime/src/kmp_settings.cpp:2034-2207. The packet name __kmp_parse_proclist does not exist in the OpenMP runtime sources (grep over the runtime directory finds nothing); the slice kmp_settings.cpp:2043-2299 contains this function, so it is fixed under its real name. Not read: SKIP_WS/SKIP_DIGITS macros, __kmp_str_to_int.

name: __kmp_stg_parse_allocator
prose: Parses the OMP_ALLOCATOR environment value (name, value) into the global __kmp_def_allocator; returns nothing. is_memalloc is true when the value contains neither "mem_space" nor ':'. Predefined-allocator form: omp_high_bw_mem_alloc and omp_large_cap_mem_alloc set __kmp_def_allocator to that allocator and return when __kmp_hwloc_available or __kmp_memkind_available is set, otherwise they warn OmpNoAllocator; omp_const/low_lat/cgroup/pteam/thread_mem_alloc warn OmpNoAllocator; omp_default_mem_alloc and every case that did not return then set __kmp_def_allocator = omp_default_mem_alloc, warn StgInvalidValue when nothing was consumed or text remains, and return. Memory-space form (value has a ':' or 'mem_space'): the memory space name (default, large_cap, const, high_bw, low_lat) is read, an unknown name sets the default allocator, warns if nothing/extra text and returns; if a ':' is present it then parses comma-separated trait=value pairs (sync_hint, alignment as a power of two, access, pool_size, fallback, pinned, partition, and fb_data= for a predefined fallback allocator). An unrecognised key, an invalid value (non-digit, non-power-of-two alignment, negative pool_size) skips that pair with a StgInvalidValue warning and reduces ntraits. At the end it calls __kmpc_init_allocator(gtid, memspace, ntraits, traits) and sets __kmp_def_allocator to the result, or omp_default_mem_alloc if that is omp_null_allocator. Not verified by running: if the value names a memory space with no ':' and non-blank text remains after it, the loop body does not advance the scan pointer on later iterations.
note: openmp/runtime/src/kmp_settings.cpp:3701-4013. Reviewer (r15) comment on warnings for unrecognized/negative trait pairs is RIGHT in the sense that the code does warn through SKIP_PAIR (:3741-3750) for those; the old prose and reviewer disagreed about it. The possible non-advancing loop (:3861-3887 with no delim) is my reading and was not tested. Partly read: __kmp_match_str, __kmp_str_match_true, __kmpc_init_allocator.

name: __kmp_release_deps
prose: Called when task `task` finishes, to release its dependences. With OMPX_TASKGRAPH, if the task belongs to a task graph that is not being recorded it decrements the predecessor counter of each recorded successor and calls __kmp_omp_task for a successor whose counter reaches 0 and whose task pointer is non-null, then returns at once, skipping the lock release, dephash free and node handling below. Otherwise: if the task's depnode exists and mtx_num_locks < 0 it makes the count positive and releases the mutexinoutset locks in reverse order; if the task has a dependence hash it frees it (__kmp_dephash_free) and clears the pointer; if there is no depnode it returns. Otherwise it acquires the depnode lock, sets node->dn.task = NULL (not done for a task-graph task that is being recorded) and releases it, then for each successor in node->dn.successors: atomically decrements its predecessor count and, if that reached 0 and the successor has a task, queues it: on a hidden-helper thread a successor that is not itself a hidden-helper task is handed to its encountering thread with __kmpc_give_task, otherwise __kmp_omp_task; on other threads __kmp_omp_task. Each list element is dereferenced and freed, and finally the task's own depnode is dereferenced. Returns nothing.
note: openmp/runtime/src/kmp_taskdeps.h:97-210 (taskgraph early return :99-112, clearing of dn.task :143-148). Reviewers RIGHT: taskgraph early return skips lock release/dephash free (original); recording task graph tasks do not have dn.task cleared (r15); zero-count successors are queued only if dn.task is non-null (:167).

name: __kmp_task_finish<ompt>
prose: Finishes execution of an explicit task `task` on thread gtid; resumed_task is the task to resume afterwards (NULL allowed for serialized tasks, then the parent is used). Pops the tied-task stack when that debug feature is built. For an untied task it atomically decrements td_untied_count and, if parts remain (count > 0), restores th_current_task to the resumed task, marks it executing and returns without completing or freeing the task. Otherwise it runs the compiler's destructor thunk if flagged. For a detachable task whose completion event is still pending (checked under the event lock) the task is marked proxy, executing is cleared and completed is false; for a task with a target async handle it is re-queued with __kmpc_give_task (signalling the hidden-helper worker when on a hidden-helper thread) and completed is false. If completed: it sets complete and onced, and when __kmp_track_children_task(taskdata) is true it releases dependences, atomically decrements the parent's incomplete-child count and the taskgroup count; otherwise, if the task team has found proxy or hidden-helper tasks, it releases dependences only; the children and taskgroup counts are not decremented in that case. Then it clears executing (after release_deps) and decrements the unexecuted hidden-helper count for hidden-helper tasks. Afterwards it sets th_current_task = resumed_task, calls __kmp_free_task_and_ancestors only if completed, marks the resumed task executing, and for task-graph tasks decrements the taskgroup count. Returns nothing; the OMPT finish callbacks are issued only when the ompt template argument is true.
note: openmp/runtime/src/kmp_tasking.cpp:1021-1235 (untied early return :1059-1072, detach :1108-1135, async :1138-1151, completion :1153-1200, free :1209-1211). Reviewers RIGHT: children/taskgroup decrement only when __kmp_track_children_task (:1166-1179), free deferred or skipped when not completed (:1210). __kmp_track_children_task at openmp/runtime/src/kmp_tasking.cpp:997-1009. Not read: __kmp_free_task_and_ancestors.

name: __kmp_invoke_task
prose: Executes task `task` on thread gtid with `current_task` as the task to resume. If the task is a proxy and already complete, it runs __kmp_bottom_half_finish_proxy and returns, skipping everything below. Otherwise: with OMPT it saves the thread's OMPT info and sets a work state; unless the task is a proxy it calls __kmp_task_start. If cancellation is enabled and the task's taskgroup has a cancel request or the team has t_cancel_request == cancel_parallel, the task is discarded (OMPT cancel callback, statistics) and its routine is not run. Otherwise (not discarded): an untied task copies td_last_tied from current_task; statistics/OMPT/OMPD/ITT bookkeeping is done; if the task has a target async handle it calls tgt_target_nowait_query on that handle instead of running the routine; else if task->routine is non-null it calls it, as routine(shareds) for a native task or routine(gtid, task). Afterwards, unless the task is a proxy, it restores the saved OMPT info (clearing the exit frame for tied tasks) and calls __kmp_task_finish (also for a discarded task); for a proxy task it only runs OMPT task-finish with ompt_task_switch when OMPT is enabled and the task has the target flag, and does not restore the OMPT state. Returns nothing.
note: openmp/runtime/src/kmp_tasking.cpp:1742-1946 (proxy early return :1751-1766, discard :1793-1813, run :1888-1904, finish :1924-1938). Reviewers RIGHT: async target handle path queries instead of running the routine and the routine may be NULL (original); proxy tasks get an OMPT finish only when the target flag is set and the OMPT state is not restored (r15).

name: lua_gc
prose: Lua C API: performs the garbage-collector operation `what` with extra arguments from the variable-argument list; returns an int. If the collector has been stopped internally (g->gcstp has GCSTPGC) it returns -1 immediately, before taking the state lock, for every option. Otherwise it takes lua_lock and handles: LUA_GCSTOP (set stopped by user; res 0), LUA_GCRESTART (debt 0, clear stop flags; 0), LUA_GCCOLLECT (full collection; 0), LUA_GCCOUNT / LUA_GCCOUNTB (total bytes >> 10, and the low 10 bits), LUA_GCSTEP (optional int argument; a basic step when 0 or adds data*1024 to the debt and checks the GC; returns 1 if a cycle finished, else 0), LUA_GCSETPAUSE / LUA_GCSETSTEPMUL (returns the old parameter and sets the new from the int argument), LUA_GCISRUNNING (gcrunning), LUA_GCGEN and LUA_GCINC (return the previous mode, update parameters that are non-zero, and change mode), and any other value returns -1 (after having locked and then unlocking). The function releases the lock (lua_unlock) before returning on all paths that took it.
note: contrib/lua/src/lapi.c:1133-1229. Reviewers RIGHT: invalid option returns -1 after taking the lock (:1224, :1227) and stopped collector returns -1 before locking (:1137-1138); old precondition text was wrong.

name: luaG_traceexec
prose: Called before each Lua opcode when debugging hooks may be active; pc points at the instruction being executed in the current Lua function. If the hook mask has neither the line nor the count bit, it clears ci->u.l.trap and returns 0. Otherwise it increments pc to refer to the next instruction and saves it in ci->u.l.savedpc, decrements L->hookcount only when the count mask is set and treats a result of 0 as a count event (reset by resethookcount). If it is not a count event and the line mask is not set it returns 1. If the previous hook yielded (CIST_HOOKYIELD) it clears that flag and returns 1 without calling hooks. It corrects L->top when the instruction does not use the top, calls the count hook (LUA_HOOKCOUNT) if due, and for the line mask calls the line hook (LUA_HOOKLINE) when the new pc index is not after the old one (a backward jump) or the line changed, then stores the new pc index in L->oldpc (L->oldpc is treated as 0 if invalid). If a hook yielded (L->status == LUA_YIELD) it undoes the count decrement (hookcount = 1 if a count event), marks CIST_HOOKYIELD and throws LUA_YIELD, so it does not return in that case. Otherwise returns 1 (keep the trap set).
note: contrib/lua/src/ldebug.c:928-970 (returns :935, :943, :946, :969; yield throw :967). Reviewers RIGHT: pc is the current instruction and is incremented (:937) (original); hookcount is decremented only when the count mask is set (:939) (r15).

name: singlestep
prose: Performs one incremental step of the Lua garbage collector and returns the amount of work done (lu_mem); the collector must not be running (asserted). It sets g->gcstopem = 1, then by g->gcstate: GCSpause: restart the collection, state becomes GCSpropagate, work 1; GCSpropagate: if the gray list is empty the state becomes GCSenteratomic (work 0), otherwise it traverses one gray object (propagatemark) and the state stays GCSpropagate; GCSenteratomic: runs atomic(), then entersweep, records the first GCestimate; the sweeping states run sweepstep, which advances to the next sweep state only when its sweep list is exhausted (not on every call); GCSswpend: checkSizes, state GCScallfin, work 0; GCScallfin: if objects remain to be finalized and not in emergency mode it clears gcstopem and runs up to GCFINMAX finalizers (state stays GCScallfin, work scaled by GCFINALIZECOST), otherwise the state becomes GCSpause with work 0. At the end it resets gcstopem to 0 and returns the work, except that an invalid state hits lua_assert(0) and returns 0 without resetting gcstopem. So the state is not advanced on every call.
note: contrib/lua/src/lgc.c:1585-1645. Reviewers RIGHT: propagate and finalizer steps may keep the same state, and the default path returns without resetting gcstopem (:1641). Partly read: sweepstep, atomic, propagatemark (only used by name).

name: fullinc
prose: Performs a full garbage collection in incremental mode. If the collector invariant is being kept (keepinvariant(g), meaning black objects may exist) it calls entersweep to turn them white. It then runs luaC_runtilstate until GCSpause (finishing any sweep in progress), runs until GCSpropagate (starts a new cycle), sets g->gcstate = GCSenteratomic directly (so the propagate phase is skipped), runs until GCScallfin (atomic phase and sweeping; the debug-only lua_assert then checks GCestimate equals the total bytes), runs until GCSpause (calls pending finalizers and finishes), and finally calls setpause(g). Finalizers run in the last step, so allocations they make may happen after that assertion point. Returns nothing.
note: contrib/lua/src/lgc.c:1710-1722. Reviewers RIGHT: the assert is evaluated before the finalizer phase (:1719-1720) and the propagate phase is skipped by the direct state assignment (:1716).

name: fts_read
prose: BSD fts compat: returns the next FTSENT of the traversal (fts_cur), or NULL at the end or on a fatal condition. It returns NULL at once if fts_cur is NULL or FTS_STOP is set. It saves and clears the current node's instruction. If the current node is a directory in pre-order (FTS_D): when the instruction is FTS_SKIP or the device changed under FTS_XDEV it frees any pending children, sets FTS_DP and returns the node for its post-order visit; otherwise it uses pending children or calls fts_build; if fts_build returns NULL it returns NULL when FTS_STOP is set, or else returns the same directory node with whatever fts_info fts_build left (FTS_DNR with fts_errno when opendir failed, FTS_DP for an empty directory, FTS_ERR on memory errors with STOP set, so the first two cases are a normal return, not an error stop); otherwise it makes the first child current, builds its path and returns it. For other nodes it moves to the next sibling (freeing the finished node): a root-level next calls fts_load and returns it; a sibling with FTS_SKIP is skipped; otherwise its path is built and it is returned. With no sibling it moves to the parent (freeing the node): the root parent ends the traversal (frees it, sets errno = 0, returns NULL); otherwise the path is truncated and the parent is returned with fts_info FTS_ERR if it has a recorded fts_errno, else FTS_DP (normal post-order visit).
note: contrib/mandoc/compat_fts.c:224-317; fts_build at :351-501 (opendir failure :370-374, empty dir :492-495). Reviewers RIGHT: FTS_DNR returns the current node (original) and the normal post-order FTS_DP return (r15).

name: getline
prose: POSIX getline replacement: reads a line from fp into *buf, growing it as needed; returns the number of characters read including the newline (excluding the NUL), or -1. If buf or bufsz is NULL it sets errno = EINVAL and returns -1. If *buf is NULL it sets *bufsz = 0, else it stores a NUL in **buf (so a non-NULL *buf must be at least one byte). It reads with fgetc; before each byte it reallocates (doubling *bufsz, or BUFSIZ from 0) whenever pos + 1 >= *bufsz, so the buffer is kept as is when it is already large enough; if realloc fails it returns -1 (earlier contents stay in the old buffer). Every stored byte is followed by a NUL. On a newline it returns the length; on EOF it NUL-terminates and returns the length if at least one character was read and feof(fp) is true, otherwise -1 (also for a read error). Bytes equal to NUL are stored and counted.
note: contrib/mandoc/compat_getline.c:25-59. Reviewers (round 1/2) RIGHT: *buf is only reallocated when more space is needed (:43-49).

name: main
prose: Entry point of mandoc / man / apropos / whatis / help. It sets the program name and, for a name beginning with mandocdb or equal to the makewhatis name, returns mandocdb(argc, argv) at once. It selects the argument mode from the program name, parses options with getopt (a usage error calls usage(), which exits), and handles option errors for -I, -K, -T, -W and -O by printing a message and returning mandoc_msg_getrc() directly, without freeing the configuration (so these early returns skip manconf_free). It resolves the output mode, applies -O (either as search output key or as manconf_output settings), decides on pager use and terminal width, and applies pledge when available. For man-style modes it applies quirks (help page default argument, a leading section argument, MACHINE for the architecture). Unless in file mode (it also does this in file mode when the message level minimum is MANDOCERR_STYLE) it fills defpaths from `manpath -q` when -M is not given and calls manconf_parse. In man mode it resolves each name separately (mansearch then fs_search), warns when nothing matches, and for first-match output picks the best section by priority; with no names and -w it prints the manpath and returns; apropos/whatis do one mansearch (usage() when it fails, 'nothing appropriate' when it finds nothing); file mode builds one entry per file argument (or stdin). Output modes -w and -l print file names or name lists and jump to cleanup; otherwise it allocates parser state, processes each result with process_onefile, reports an unused -O tag, frees the formatter data, and at `out:` frees the search results and, unless in file mode, the configuration, closes tag files and may run the pager or print the message summary. It returns mandoc_msg_getrc().
note: contrib/mandoc/main.c:124-687 (function head at :124; slice 302-584 is the middle). Reviewers RIGHT: early -O error return skips manconf_free (:374-376) (r15); config is also read in file mode when the minimum message level is MANDOCERR_STYLE (:463-466) (r17). Partly read: helper functions (process_onefile, fs_search, mansearch, run_pager) not read.

name: print_man_node
prose:
HTML output of one man(7) node n. It returns immediately, printing nothing, for a comment node or a node flagged NODE_NOPRT. Otherwise it sets the fill mode from NODE_NOFILL (and may end the line in no-fill mode). Text nodes: an empty string prints an end-of-line and returns; otherwise a leading blank at the start of an input line emits a
(unless HTML_NONEWLINE), a delimiter-closing flag sets no-space, the tag's refcount is incremented and the text is printed. Equation nodes are printed with print_eqn. Table nodes are printed with print_tbl and the function returns. For other nodes it closes any font scope, closes an open table, increments the current tag's refcount, and if the token is a roff request (n->tok < ROFF_MAX) it calls roff_html_pre, restores the refcount, closes tags with print_stagq and returns without printing children; otherwise it calls the macro's pre handler (when present), whose result decides whether the children are printed. After the children it decrements the refcount; for IP/TP/TQ blocks it finds the enclosing DL/UL tag and closes the whole list if no further item of that type follows, else only the item. Returns nothing. The early returns for comments/NOPRT, empty text, tables and roff requests skip the final refcount decrement and tag closing.
note: contrib/mandoc/man_html.c:164-262 (returns :171, :185, :208, :232). Reviewers RIGHT: early returns skip printing and refcount handling (original) and the roff-macro branch (n->tok < ROFF_MAX) (:228-233) (r15).

name: manconf_output
prose: Parses one -O style output option string cp into the manoutput structure conf; fromfile is non-zero when it comes from the config file. Returns 0 on success and -1 after printing a message on error. It matches cp against the tokens includes, man, paper, style, indent, width, outfilename, tagfilename, tag, fragment, noval, toc (a token must be followed by a blank, '=' or the end), skips an '=' and following blanks, and handles: the first eight need a non-empty value (otherwise BADVAL_MISS, -1); fragment, noval and toc must have no value (otherwise BADVAL, -1); an unknown option gives BADARG_BAD, -1. Setting rules: includes, man, paper, style, outfilename, tagfilename and tag store a copy of the value when not yet set; if already set, the old value is kept, and the call returns 0 silently when fromfile, or reports BADVAL_DUPE and returns -1 otherwise. indent (0..1000) and width (1..1000) use strtonum and report BADVAL_BAD with -1 for bad numbers; they are treated as already set only when the stored value is non-zero. fragment, noval and toc just set their flag to 1 and return 0, with no duplicate detection.
note: contrib/mandoc/manpath.c:212-349 (function head at :212; slice 302-349 is the tail). Reviewer (r17) RIGHT: flag options are not duplicate-checked (:327-335). Earlier round names this an unnamed -O option parser; real name manconf_output.

name: args
prose: Static tokenizer in mdoc_argv.c that scans the next argument of an mdoc macro line from buf at *pos and returns an enum margserr, storing the argument start in *v (a local dummy when v is NULL). If at end of line it returns ARGS_EOLN, first warning ARG_QUOTE and clearing PHRASELIT if a quoted literal is still open outside a phrase, and clearing PHRASEQL. With flag ARGSFL_DELIM and a line whose remaining words are a close delimiter followed only by delimiters it returns ARGS_PUNCT. With ARGSFL_TABSEP it takes the field up to the next tab (or to the end of the line), updates PHRASEQL/PHRASEQN, skips blanks after the tab and trailing blanks, NUL-terminates in place and returns ARGS_PHRASE. If a quoted literal is open (MDOC_PHRASELIT) or the phrase flag is set and the word begins with '"', it parses a quoted literal in place: the opening quote is skipped, doubled quotes collapse to one, an unescaped closing quote ends it and is replaced by NUL; if the line ends first it warns ARG_QUOTE (unless in a phrase) and leaves PHRASELIT set; in all these quoted cases it returns ARGS_WORD, after skipping following blanks and warning SPACE_EOL if the line then ends. Otherwise it takes the word with roff_getarg (a newly allocated string, freed here when v was NULL), converts PHRASEQL to PHRASEQF after the last word of a phrase, and returns ARGS_ALLOC (the caller must free *v).
note: contrib/mandoc/mdoc_argv.c:444-589 (head at :444; slice 521-682 starts mid-function). Reviewer (r15) RIGHT on ARGS_WORD handling (the literal case returns ARGS_WORD with the flag state described, :529-571). Partly read: roff_getarg, args_checkpunct (read), mdoc_isdelim not read.

name: print_word
prose: Writes the word s to standard output for the man(7) generator, using the file-level flags outflags and counter TPremain. If any pending break flag (MMAN_PP, sp, br, nl) is set it prints the corresponding request line (.PP with .PD bookkeeping, .sp, .br or a plain newline), clears those flags and MMAN_spc, prints '.br' if TPremain == 1, sets TPremain = 0, and prints no space before the word. Otherwise, if MMAN_spc is set, it prints a space (preceded by a backslash for a non-suspended Bk word) only if the space is forced, s is empty, s does not start with one of .,:;)]?! or s is longer than one character; a printed space decrements TPremain if non-zero. It then recomputes MMAN_spc (set when MMAN_Sm is on and s is not a lone '(' or '['), clears the force and Bk-suspend flags, and prints the characters: ASCII_NBRSP as '\ ', ASCII_HYPH as '-', ASCII_BREAK as '\:', a blank as '\ ' when MMAN_nbrword is set, else the character; TPremain is decremented (if non-zero) once per input character of s, not per output character. Finally it clears MMAN_nbrword. Returns nothing.
note: contrib/mandoc/mdoc_man.c:378-460. Reviewers RIGHT: TPremain counts input characters (:456-457) (original); no space after pending break flags and the extra .br when TPremain == 1 (:403-404) (r15).

name: print_node
prose: Recursive man(7) output for one mdoc node. It returns immediately for a node flagged NODE_NOPRT. It sets MMAN_nl when a space is pending, the node starts a line and is not transparent, and clears NODE_ENDED on the node at entry (so already-ended nodes are processed). Equation and table nodes print a notice that -T man does not support them and return. Text nodes get a leading '\&' when a line starts with '.' or ''', spacing flags are adjusted for delimiters and Sm, and the text is printed with print_word. Other nodes: a roff request (n->tok < ROFF_MAX) is handled by roff_man_acts and the function returns without visiting children or running post handlers; an mdoc macro looks up its action, evaluates its condition, runs its pre handler when the condition holds and (n->end == ENDBODY_NOT or the node has children), whose result decides whether children are visited. The children are visited recursively. If NODE_ENDED has been set on the node by then (e.g. by an enclosing block end) it returns without running the post handler or marking the body; otherwise it runs the post handler when the condition held and, for an end-of-body node (n->end != ENDBODY_NOT), sets NODE_ENDED on n->body. Returns nothing.
note: contrib/mandoc/mdoc_man.c:641-731 (return sites :648, :676, :701, :724). Reviewers RIGHT: NODE_ENDED cleared at entry (:662) and NODE_NOPRT is an early return, not a precondition (original); early return when NODE_ENDED is set after the children (:723-724) (r15).

name: state_sh
prose: mdoc state handler for the Sh macro. It does nothing unless n is the head of the block (n->type == ROFFT_HEAD). If the node is not yet marked NODE_VALID it determines the section: a head with exactly one text child maps through mdoc_a2sec, otherwise SEC_CUSTOM; it stores that in the parent block's sec and sets it with setsec(n, sec). Regardless of NODE_VALID it then sets mdoc->lastsec = n->sec; if that is SEC_SYNOPSIS it sets the roff register nS to 1 and the MDOC_SYNOPSIS flag, otherwise it sets nS to 0 and clears that flag. Returns nothing.
note: contrib/mandoc/mdoc_state.c:228-249. Reviewers RIGHT: the section assignment is guarded by NODE_VALID (:235) (original), and lastsec/nS/MDOC_SYNOPSIS updates happen also when NODE_VALID is set (:242-248) (r15).

name: termp_sh_pre
prose: Terminal renderer pre-handler for the Sh macro; returns 1 in all branches except the head, where it returns the result of termp_bold_pre. For the block it calls term_vspace(p) unless the previous sibling is an Sh whose body is empty (a previous Sh with an empty body suppresses the vertical space). For the head it sets p->fontibi = 1 and returns termp_bold_pre(p, pair, meta, n). For the body it sets p->tcol->offset = term_len(p, p->defindent), resets the tab stops (term_tab_set NULL, then "T" and ".5i"), and for the AUTHORS section clears the TERMP_SPLIT and TERMP_NOSPLIT flags. Other node types change nothing.
note: contrib/mandoc/mdoc_term.c:1266-1296. Reviewers RIGHT: vertical spacing for BLOCK and the fontibi side effect for HEAD (original); BODY offset is term_len(p, p->defindent), not p->defindent (:1285) (r15).

name: tblcalc_number
prose: Computes and records the width of one numeric table cell in out.c. Returns 0 for a null or empty cell string. Otherwise totsz is the printed width of the string (tbl->slen). If col is NULL it returns totsz without touching any column. With a column it looks for the last digit and the last decimal point adjacent to a digit (the \& alignment mark overrides both); if there is no digit it treats the cell as a literal string, raises col->width to totsz when smaller and returns totsz. Otherwise it measures the integer part width intsz up to the decimal point (or after the last digit); if intsz exceeds col->decimal it increases col->nwidth by the difference and sets col->decimal = intsz, else it adds col->decimal - intsz to totsz; then it raises col->nwidth to totsz and col->width to col->nwidth when smaller, and returns totsz (including the alignment padding).
note: contrib/mandoc/out.c:497-570 (slice 519-570 is the tail; head at :497). Reviewer (r17) WRONG: the numeric path does handle col == NULL, returning totsz at :510-511 before any dereference of col.
